name: I Can't Believe I Did It
note: Fill your life with stories that start with "I can't believe I did it" — not the ones that start with "I wish I did it."
desc: A nudge to bias toward action: the leaps and risks you actually take become the stories you're proud of later, while the ones you talk yourself out of just turn into quiet regrets.

name: A Mind Opened by Wonder
note: Curiosity beats certainty — a closed mind only protects the length of your life, not its depth.
desc: A longevity stack can extend the years, but an open, wonder-driven mind is what makes them worth living — a gentle argument for staying curious over staying certain.

name: The Greatest Sin
note: Knowing exactly what you want and never acting on it may be the costliest form of self-sabotage.
desc: The hardest part of any stack usually isn't knowing what works — it's actually doing it. A reminder that clarity without action helps no one, least of all future you.
